bindings.label: Development of an epiretinal membrane in the right eye

Woman in her 70s with pseudophakia and history of chronic noninfectious bilateral uveitis and recurrent cystoid macular edema was being treated with serial injections of 0.7-mg dexamethasone intravitreal implants
Best-corrected visual acuity was approximately 20/50 OD and 20/200 OS
One week after the initial procedure: visual acuity was 20/100 OD, intraocular pressure was 10 mm Hg, there was 40% to 50% gas fill, and the retina was attached
Fundus photo and raster scan reveal dexamethasone implant adherent to retina with indentation and compression of retinal layers
Raster scan demonstrates hyperautofluorescence of the retinal layers
Dexamethasone implant was found adherent to the retina five days after vitrectomy
Raster scan shows linear hyperautofluorescence with compression in the superior macula
